sections.label: Budget cut for Head F
sections.summary: A motion is moved to reduce the total sum allocated for Head F of the Estimates by $100, stating Parliament is where Government authority stems.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head F of the Estimates be reduced by $100." In our country's governance, Parliament is where the authority of the Government stems.

sections.label: Ministerial Statements and Parliamentary Committees
sections.summary: Ministerial Statements allow only short clarifications and no debate, while Parliamentary Committees give Parliament regular public dialogue and input.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For example, questions about Ridout Road and the initial announcement of former Transport Minister S Iswaran being investigated by the Corrupt Practices Investigation Bureau (CPIB) were taken by way of Ministerial Statements in July and August 2023 respectively.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A Ministerial Statement only allows for Members to ask short clarifications and the Standing Orders expressly prohibit Members from having a debate thereon.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While a full Motion means that any Member wanting to make their views known on the matter have up to 20 minutes to make a speech, not including clarifications, a means through which Parliament obtains regular and better dialogue and input from the public is by the use of Parliamentary Committees, which my colleague Gerald Giam will speak on.

sections.label: Seven standing Select Committees
sections.summary: Parliament currently has seven standing Select Committees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Parliament currently has seven standing Select Committees.

sections.label: Proposed standing Select Committees for Ministries
sections.summary: A call is made to set up standing Select Committees for each Ministry or related Ministries, with MPs from all parties and Parliament Secretariat support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For these reasons, I call on Parliament to set up standing Select Committees for each Ministry or group of related Ministries, consisting of MPs from all political parties represented in Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: They should be supported by the Parliament Secretariat and meeting minutes should be made available to all committee members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Ministries should endeavour to engage them on a regular basis.

sections.label: Concern over deterring good people
sections.summary: A citizen is concerned that changing demands will deter good people who should be in Government, given Singapore's limited talent pool.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore is a small country with a limited talent pool and as a citizen, I am concerned that many of our good people who should be in Government will be deterred by these changing demands.

sections.label: Passion to serve and competence
sections.summary: The cardinal criteria are a genuine passion to serve and a high level of competence, not infallibility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To me, the cardinal criteria are a genuine passion to serve and a high level of competence – not infallibility.

sections.label: Corruptible traits fatal to MPs
sections.summary: A corruptible character and a proclivity towards dishonesty are traits fatal to a good MP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A corruptible character and a proclivity towards dishonesty are traits that are fatal to a good MP.

sections.label: Praise and loss of privacy
sections.summary: Praising MPs for good work does no harm, but loss of privacy is a big deterrent to entering politics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But just like anyone else, it does not harm to give them a pat on the back when they do a good job and I am sure they will appreciate it and be spurred on to do better.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But this loss of privacy is, in my view, one of the biggest deterrents to persons entering into politics.

sections.label: Asset declarations by Ministers and MPs
sections.summary: Ministers declare private assets to the President routinely, and in the UK all MPs declare assets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, Ministers do have to declare their private assets to the President and on a routine basis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In his own example – the UK – all MPs, including opposition MPs, have to declare their assets, not only Ministers.

sections.label: Town Councils and conflicts of interest
sections.summary: Town Councils handle tens of millions of dollars in contracts yearly, so conflicts of interest for backbencher MPs are possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Town Councils handle tens of millions of dollars of contracts every year, so the potential for conflicts of interest to arise for backbencher MPs is also quite possible.

sections.label: MPs' work and attracting MPs
sections.summary: What is relevant is MPs' actual work and impact, but the concern is the effect of these suggestions on attracting MPs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What is relevant is the actual work and impact of MPs on the ground, as I have mentioned earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But my concern today, is the effect of these suggestions on attracting persons to become MPs – both for the ruling party as well as for the opposition.

sections.label: Why Ministerial Statements were used
sections.summary: Issues were taken by Ministerial Statement as the normal way to present information, and this does not preclude a Motion.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: On the question of why certain issues were taken by way of Ministerial Statement, those were taken by way of Ministerial Statement because that is the normal way in which information is presented to Parliament, and Members had the opportunity to ask questions, which they did.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We did not do it by way of a Motion, simply because it did not present itself as a matter for resolution, but this does not preclude anybody else from raising a Motion if they wish to.

sections.label: More committees not productive
sections.summary: Having more Standing Committees or Select Committees would not be very productive.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Having more Standing Committees or more Select Committees would not be very productive.

sections.label: Standing Select Committees accountability limits
sections.summary: Creating standing Select Committees for every Ministry would do little to enhance accountability, productivity or efficiency, as shown by the Select Committee on Deliberate Online Falsehoods.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: For these reasons, creating standing Select Committees for every Ministry would do little to enhance accountability or increase productivity or efficiency.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: One example is the Select Committee on Deliberate Online Falsehoods, which Ms He also mentioned, that was appointed in 2018 to study what was then, and still is, a new and complex societal problem.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: To examine this one policy issue – just this one, not even the work of the entire Ministry – the Committee held 16 meetings over eight months, conducted public consultations with many stakeholders, and received written representations and oral evidence from individuals and organisations alike, before reporting its findings to Parliament.

sections.label: Integrity and honesty bright line
sections.summary: Mistakes will occasionally be made and dealt with, but integrity and honesty require a bright white line because citizens must trust Parliament.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Occasionally, some mistakes will be made and those would have to be dealt with, but where we have to draw a bright white line is where integrity and honesty are concerned, because the people and our citizens must be able to trust us.

sections.label: Effective platform for rigorous debates
sections.summary: The platform remains effective for rigorous debates on important issues and will evolve with changing needs, reflecting the resilience of the democratic institution.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: So, I thank Mr Thomas for his remarks.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: It remains an effective platform for rigorous debates on important issues and it will continue to evolve in tandem with our changing needs, and this speaks to the resilience of our democratic institution.

sections.label: Select Committees do not guarantee governance
sections.summary: Select Committees do not necessarily guarantee or give better governance or better accountability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: I assume that the reason why the Member suggests having Select Committees is: he feels it would make for better governance and that it would make for better accountability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: I am saying that having Select Committees does not necessarily guarantee nor give you better governance or better accountability.

sections.label: Parliamentary Committees not Parliament Committee
sections.summary: They are called Parliamentary Committees, but they are not a Parliament Committee.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: I am afraid the Member may have it back to front.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: They are called "Parliamentary Committees", but they are not a "Parliament Committee".

sections.label: Purpose of GPCs
sections.summary: The GPCs let the dominant ruling party help Government MPs perform duties better and play a more effective policy-making role.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The purpose of the GPCs was to allow the ruling party, which was the dominant party, to enable or to help the Government's MPs to perform their duties better, by playing a more effective role in the policy-making process, to tap on their expertise and to allow them to give political feedback.

sections.label: GPCs' role
sections.summary: The GPCs scrutinise legislation, make suggestions to the Minister, and help Ministries do better.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Essentially, the GPCs' role is to scrutinise legislation, to make suggestions to the Minister, and to help the Ministries to do better.

sections.label: Thanks to Parliament staff
sections.summary: The speaker thanks Parliament staff for running Parliamentary business, visiting dignitaries, overseas visits, security, research, communications and facilities management.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: To close, I would like to thank Parliament staff for their work in ensuring the running of the various different functions of Parliament, which range from the official Parliamentary business, like ensuring that Sittings go smoothly, coordinating visiting dignitaries and overseas visits, and also, the often unseen work in ensuring the functioning of areas, such as security, research, communications and facilities management.

sections.label: Thomas Paine and strong Parliament
sections.summary: Citing Thomas Paine, the speaker urges members to maintain a strong Parliament for future generations and withdraws the amendment.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: This brings to mind something that Thomas Paine said a few centuries ago, in which he reminded us that there can never exist a Parliament which will last forever, nor capable of commanding forever how to govern.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: So, given that our time on earth and this Chamber, is temporal, I hope that all of us can look deep within ourselves to think about the part that we can do in the here and now, to maintain an institution that can be rightfully called a strong Parliament that future generations can look up to.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: Chairman, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
